## Selected relationships and references

- Organization → recursive team tree; each employee has one home team. A lead is a direct member appointed to manage the subtree; an ordinary ancestor-team member gains no such authority. Explicit person-to-person reporting remains distinct.
- A project requires one accountable owner team and may have contributing teams. Teams/projects are organization-wide; offices place agents, not teams/projects.
- A task always has an accountable team and optionally a project. Task/bug/request are task types, all using T- references. Assignment is independent of accountable ownership. Preserve old stable IDs and resolve old B-/REQ- references through explicit migration mappings, never by stripping/reusing the number.
- TEAM- and P- counters are organization-scoped; T- is project-scoped or team-scoped when projectless; F-/R- are project-scoped; M- belongs to its release. Slugs/handles follow document 06. Organization/office IDs do not get new human counters.
- A repository is registered once under the organization and may be shared by projects. Integration branches belong to each project/repository association, never to the organization cache. Local code repositories are supported; the organization metadata repository itself must be remote.
- Features use project-prefixed slugs and stable-ID file paths in organization Git. Feature definitions explain behavior/limitations; supporting project/feature/release/deployment documents have the ownership defined in document 02. Release product changelogs and deployment technical changelogs remain distinct.
- A built-in HR agent is an employee and therefore requires a home team; bootstrap must choose a valid team explicitly before admitting the profile. Its special chart placement is presentation, not an identity exception.
- An authenticated owner account remains a security principal. If represented by an employee/person record, that record has the same required home-team constraint; displaying the owner above the chart does not create a teamless employee or grant authority from a YAML flag.

## Folder and privacy boundaries

Portable definitions/open work live in organization Git; task work and code live in runtime worktrees. Supporting knowledge uses a required project scope and at most one same-project feature/release/deployment scope. Release content and intended flags are authored records; deployment commit/flag snapshots record what was actually applied. These fields do not implement deployment or flag evaluation. Protected chat, budget amounts/history, private notes, usage archives, command receipts and recovery evidence are not made public by putting their SQL projection in one draft schema. Each source's visibility and durability boundary still applies. Private task notes
are author-only by default, including against organization owners/administrators;
existing shared note comments are not private. Published task history is immutable
shared evidence and must contain no private-note body or identifying metadata.

The target runtime layout is defined by [employee structure](organization-data/04-agent-structure.md#runtime-location):

```text
runtime/<office-id>/
├── repositories/<repository-id>.git/              # cache, no project integration branch
└── teams/<root-team-id>/teams/<child-team-id>/.../
    └── agents/<employee-id>/
        ├── projects/<project-id>/tasks/<task-id>/repositories/<repository-id>/
        └── tasks/<task-id>/repositories/<repository-id>/   # projectless task
```

Workspaces survive handoff until task closure; changing current agent/office placement requires an explicit safe workspace migration, not recursive deletion. This diagram defines ownership, not a completed sandbox migration. Re-derive Git metadata, credential, other-task and managed-state denies for the target paths and verify them before launching against that layout. Do not transplant old allowlists based on a renamed prefix.

Deleting an office cache is safe only with protected acknowledged sources, rebindable credentials and process reconciliation. A Git checkout alone does not restore chat, budgets, usage or authority. Preserve live Phase A asks/replies/triage until the separately verified transport cutover.

The referenced costs-and-budgets-v1 PRD is not present in this repository. It cannot silently override available reviewed contracts. Preserve its references as historical context; do not invent its absent decision tables. Uncovered rules stay pending explicit decisions.

Historical commit links, retired wire examples, required signing identifiers/key namespaces and installed legacy CLI instructions are evidence, not current source/package naming. ## Shared identity contract

Every entity keeps an immutable stable `id`, used for foreign keys, synchronization and filenames. New records use UUIDv7; preserve existing v1 IDs exactly without regenerating or reformatting them. Readable identifiers never replace stable IDs.

| Entity | Readable identifier | Uniqueness / counter scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Organization | `slug`, e.g. `restaurant-saas` | Organization catalog; no counter |
| Office | `slug`, e.g. `hq` | Organization; no counter |
| Agent or person | `handle`, displayed as `@ana` | Organization, shared across both employee kinds; no counter |
| Team | `TEAM-12` | Team counter within organization |
| Project | `P-8` and `slug`, e.g. `reservations` | Project counter and slug uniqueness within organization |
| Task of any type | `T-42` | Task counter within project, or within team when projectless |
| Feature | `F-6` and full slug `reservations/table-booking` | Feature counter and `local_slug` within project; full slug unique within organization |
| Release | `R-3` and optional text `version_label` | Release counter within project |
| Milestone | `M-2` | Milestone counter within release |
| Repository, role, provider connection or model profile | Descriptive `key` | Organization, separately per entity type; no counter |

Numbered records persist `number`; SQL derives `key` as the prefix plus number. The canonical file does not need a duplicate `key`; if supplied on import it must match. `number: null` denotes a locally created task/feature awaiting allocation, or an unresolved import and exposes no final readable reference. A record accepted by the organization authority must have a number and a durable allocation; local tasks/features can be used by stable ID while registration is pending. Separate scopes can both contain `T-42`: use `P-8/T-42` or `TEAM-12/T-42` outside an already selected scope. Changing task type never changes its ID or number.

Slugs are lowercase kebab-case identifiers; handles are lowercase identifiers using letters, digits, dots, underscores or hyphens, stored without `@`. They are explicit fields rather than values recalculated when display names change. Teams need no additional slug. Projects have both a numeric reference and an organization-unique slug. Features store `local_slug`, and their public `slug` is automatically derived as `<project.slug>/<feature.local_slug>`. Never manually enter the project prefix on a feature. The resulting path is unique within the organization because both component scopes enforce uniqueness. Release version labels are plain text, not an enforced semantic-version type or identity.

`schema_version` selects the file format; `revision` is the entity's concurrency revision. Dates/timestamps are quoted strings in YAML. Domain rows inherit `organization_id` from `organization.yaml`. Nested comments, checklist steps, watchers, questions and waiting spans have stable IDs without counters. Task events retain the stable `(organization_id, task_id, revision)` identity described in document 05; revisions are not another readable-number allocation. See [identity and numbering](06-identity-and-numbering.md) for allocation, durability and index contracts.

The organization repository must be remote. Its tracked content is mirrored as ordinary durable local files. Code repositories may be remote or local-only. All active Git clones and worktrees live under runtime.

```text

├── durable/
│   ├── state/                 # Latest organization repository content
│   ├── accounting/            # Durable usage streams/checkpoints; separately backed up
│   ├── authority/             # Durable numbering ledger and recovery journal
│   ├── journal/               # Pending local persistence; not Git content
│   ├── local/offices/         # Machine-specific bindings; not Git content
│   └── checkpoints/           # Local-only/unpushed code recovery bundles and edits
└── runtime/<office-id>/
    ├── office.db              # Projection + explicitly transient state
    ├── repositories/          # One bare clone per repository used by this office
    └── teams/<team-id>/.../agents/<employee-id>/
        ├── projects/<project-id>/tasks/<task-id>/repositories/<repository-id>/
        └── tasks/<task-id>/repositories/<repository-id>/  # Team tasks
```

Durable scalar values are explicit YAML/front-matter fields. Association rows come from ID arrays or maps in their owning documents. Markdown bodies map to `body_markdown`. Array positions and resolver indexes are derived and have no independently authored source. Generated numeric keys are derived from persisted numbers. Null optional fields and documented defaults round-trip identically.

Shared SQLite is the indexed projection for domain records, task activity and accounting events. The private-note database is an explicit separate durable store, not a reconstructible shared cache. Published task activity lives in organization Git under `work-history/tasks/`; acknowledged unpublished changes also require their durable journal. Accounting recovery additionally requires the durable usage archive; rates alone or organization Git alone cannot restore accounting per-event history. Cache paths and worktree paths are transient. Document 11 requires durable placement/fencing evidence before execution; recreating an office database does not authorize starting another copy of an agent. Existing authentication/credential storage remains a separate subsystem and is not made disposable by this schema. Shared organization files do not contain credentials, private task notes or chat bodies. Document 15 defines protected messaging sources outside disposable office caches; Git alone does not restore chat.

Structural import validation rejects duplicate IDs, invalid references, team cycles, path/field mismatches and a team lead outside that team's direct membership. A lead manages the team's entire subtree; ordinary members gain no management authority from their location. This describes the relationship only, not tool permissions or authorization implementation.

Saving files and Git publication remain separate. Hourly pending-work publication and prompt important-knowledge publication are publication targets, not a newly implemented sync engine. Offices host agents and cache organization data; they do not own teams, projects or counters. HQ creates teams, projects, releases and milestones. Tasks and features may be created and durably saved in any office, including while disconnected. Offices submit their stable IDs and scopes to the shared organization authority for final number allocation and feature-slug registration; they never increment replicated counters independently. Numbering recovery must preserve every acknowledged allocation; hourly Git publication alone cannot provide that guarantee.

   126	Journal records are ordered UTF-8 JSON transaction envelopes: `{schema_version, sequence, operation_id, payload_sha256, mutations, response, envelope_sha256}`. Write a complete transaction to a temporary file, durably flush it, atomically rename to its sequence name, then durably flush the parent directory before acknowledgement. All journal, ownership and input/checkpoint flushes in this document must provide the platform power-loss guarantees of [ADR-0002](../../adr/0002-storage-sqlite-sqlcipher-one-writer.md), including the macOS full-flush operation; plain fsync alone is insufficient there. Mutations contain full same-named row snapshots or explicit projection removals. A projector applies each sequence once in one SQLite transaction; a gap or checksum conflict blocks new execution until recovered. `envelope_sha256` hashes the entire canonical envelope except itself, including mutations and response, for every transaction. `payload_sha256` remains the command digest and is not an envelope-integrity check. Verify the envelope digest before replay. Asynchronous fact transactions use null operation_id, payload_sha256 and response and create no command receipt, but still require envelope_sha256. Input/checkpoint/tool files referenced by a transaction are fsynced before publishing it. Canonical JSON expands defaults/nulls, sorts keys and uses compact UTF-8 encoding; digests use the [accounting](10-usage-and-cost-accounting.md) SHA-256 convention.

   136	For the focused data-structure view—concepts, field diagrams, relationships, canonical files, examples and SQL mapping—see [Model providers, connections and pools](14-model-providers-and-connection-pools.md). It describes the same records as this execution contract.

   140	For `subscription_cli`, `subscription_identity` is required: the provider adapter's canonical, non-secret identity for the actual subscription entitlement/quota account, not a connection label, credential path, model name or office ID. HQ registers it once per `(organization_id, provider_type, subscription_identity)`. Two different connection IDs for that same subscription are rejected with `SUBSCRIPTION_ALREADY_REGISTERED`, returning the existing connection ID. Disabled/archived definitions also reserve their identity; reuse/re-enable the existing definition. One connection may appear in several profiles and have one local binding per office, while all those uses share its HQ permit/cooldown state. Multiple subscription connections in a pool represent distinct subscriptions.
   141	
   142	Identity normalization and registration happen before creating the default profile. Provider adapters use a canonical provider namespace and verified subscription identity; if the provider exposes no identity API, an explicit operator-attested mapping to the registered subscription is required. Unverified aliases cannot become runnable routes. SQL enforces uniqueness of the registered identity, but cannot prove that two credential sets reach the same external account. Bind/refresh must compare account evidence with the registered identity and return `SUBSCRIPTION_IDENTITY_MISMATCH` on a different subscription, or `SUBSCRIPTION_IDENTITY_UNVERIFIED` without evidence/attestation. These states are not ready. Credential rotation preserves identity; changing the subscription requires selecting/registering its own connection. API/cloud connections that do not represent a subscription leave this field null; this rule does not claim to identify all provider-wide API rate-limit groups.
   143	
   144	Connection creation is one idempotent organization transaction: create the connection, an auto-generated model profile, and its one membership. The profile records generated_for_connection_id. Exactly one generated default is allowed per connection. Auto-generated profiles contain exactly their source connection; converting one to a manual pool clears the generated designation in that same revisioned transaction. Profile membership is 1..64 connections in contiguous priority order. Reorder by replacing the membership set inside one transaction, then validate before commit; do not perform individually visible priority swaps.
   145	
   146	Archiving or deleting an assigned profile returns `PROFILE_IN_USE` with affected employee IDs. Referenced connections cannot be deleted through a membership cascade. Other provider/auth-mode/driver/endpoint changes are revisioned and must preserve any registered subscription identity; a supervisor never mutates a live child's environment to adopt them. Missing execution config means an employee is not runnable, not that the framework chooses a default model.

   204	## 5. Commands and admission
   205	
   206	The office exposes execution operations through its existing authenticated service boundary and dispatches typed commands to the internal supervisor. There is no additional supervisor socket, framing protocol or server-to-supervisor service credential. Existing local IPC and federation transports retain their own framing and peer admission. Execution command content is bounded to 1 MiB; larger inputs use approved immutable local content references. Validate the admitted principal, organization, office and operation scope before internal dispatch. An employee token permits only the operations explicitly authorized for that employee; it is not host administration authority.
   207	
   208	Every internal command envelope contains `{protocol_version:1, organization_id, office_id, operation_id, command, payload, payload_sha256}`; protocol_version is the internal execution-contract version, independent of existing transport API versions. Validate scope/authentication before admission. payload_sha256 hashes canonical `{command, organization_id, office_id, payload}` only; transport capabilities and worker generation are excluded so an original operation can be retried after restart. Mutation payloads include expected object revisions/placement generation; responses are `{operation_id, outcome, code, data}`. Journal the result and associated state atomically before replying. Same ID/digest returns the original response; same ID/different payload returns `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT` without side effects. A lost acknowledgement is resolved by `GetOperation(operation_id)` or the same-ID retry, never a newly generated command. Keep receipts while their turn/process/config revision is retained; no time-only dedupe expiry is introduced.

   210	| Command | Required payload / result |
   211	| --- | --- |
   212	| `RunTurn` | turn_id, employee_id, placement_generation, expected_agent_config_revision, expected_profile_revision, task_id or null, workspace_key, immutable input_ref/input_sha256. Returns accepted turn identity. A second open turn for the employee returns BUSY. |
   213	| `ResumeTurn` | turn_id, expected_turn_revision; recovery-required turns also require recovery `{checkpoint_ref, receipt_dispositions:[{operation_id, outcome, result_ref, evidence_ref}]}`. Outcome is confirmed_completed or confirmed_not_started, with evidence verified by the tool broker/operator recovery authority. Unknown outcomes remain recovery_required. Retries a blocked turn or resumes only after validated reconciliation. Preserves turn ID, model and workspace. |
   214	| `CancelTurn` | turn_id, expected_turn_revision. Stops current work and becomes cancelled only after completion/cleanup facts are known. |
   215	| `StopAgent` | employee_id, placement_generation. Stops active and idle main processes. It creates no future automatic wake or budget policy. |
   216	| `BindConnection` | connection_id, expected_binding_revision, local credential reference, verified executable path where required. Invalidates observations. Raw credentials use the local auth broker, not this payload. |
   217	| `RefreshConnection` | connection_id. Returns refreshed status/catalog or structured unavailable status. Never starts an employee LLM turn. |
   218	| Queries | GetOperation, GetTurn, GetAgentReadiness, ListProfileModels. Queries have no mutation receipt and expose no secret values. |

   220	The office validates placement/config revisions and dispatches through the internal supervisor against the same admitted snapshot. No new starts occur while the worker is stopping, recovering or has lost its host-control authority. The existing host/worker launch contract controls that lifecycle; there is no separate server-to-supervisor lease. HQ turn-permit renewal remains mandatory under §6. Unresolved cleanup retains the process/turn slot. Client deadlines of 10 seconds are response deadlines only; they do not prove a command failed or cancel accepted work.

Large content uses content-addressed local references; it is not embedded past the frame limit. Resolve paths against the office's approved roots and reject traversal/symlink substitution. The same turn keeps its original target model, profile order, workspace and input digest through every attempt. Connection disabling, revoked authority and invalid credentials override old eligibility; ordinary profile/prompt changes take effect on the next turn.    224	## 6. Shared quota and deterministic selection
   225	
   226	HQ's organization service is the single permit/cooldown coordinator. It journals before acknowledging and updates its projection in one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction: expire overdue active permits to release_pending; read connection and applicable model cooldowns; count active plus release_pending permits; grant only below max_concurrent_turns. Permission to proceed is a scoped opaque permit ID bound to employee/office/placement/model and coordinator generation. There is no global counter on the agent and no quota authority in an office's cached healthy flag.
   227	
   228	Permits last 60 seconds and renew every 10 seconds while a model turn is active. Compute local deadlines conservatively from the monotonic request-send time and the returned remaining duration. Start stop/recovery with at least 20 seconds remaining when renewal fails. **Expiry does not free capacity:** release_pending continues to count until a supervisor proves the model turn ended with no outstanding work, or proves its process/descendants gone. Unknown cleanup is not a release acknowledgement. Warm verified-idle processes consume no turn permit. Coordinator restart replays its journal and marks prior active permits release_pending before issuing new permits; affected supervisors stop/reconcile rather than reusing an old coordinator generation.
   229	
   230	A 429/quota failure is connection-wide unless verified provider evidence identifies a model-specific window. Use the provider reset/Retry-After value when present; otherwise cooldown is 900 seconds. Cooldown expiry permits another guarded attempt if local auth/entitlement evidence is still fresh; it is not an assertion that quota is known available. Unsupported quota probes leave quota status unknown and can still obtain a bounded permit, with that uncertainty exposed. Auth-expired is an office-binding observation until verified reauthentication. Never convert a tool/policy denial into permission to try a less restrictive driver.
   231	
   232	For each RunTurn/ResumeTurn dispatch cycle:
   233	
   234	1. Read the frozen ordered pool and admitted policy. Reject archived profile, disabled execution config, inactive employee or stale placement.
   235	2. In ascending priority, check connection enabled/non-archived, local binding, exact binding revision, installed driver/verified version, fresh auth readiness, confirmed model entitlement and policy/tool/context compatibility. Unknown/stale evidence produces a skip code and asynchronous refresh, not hot-path discovery.
   236	3. Ask HQ for a turn permit. A full/cooling-down connection is skipped; coordinator unavailability blocks dispatch rather than bypassing global admission.
   237	4. Reserve the employee's exclusive process slot. Reuse an idle process only if connection, driver/version, canonical model, workspace and launch digest match. The digest covers connection definition revision/endpoint, canonical and resolved model IDs, driver version/executable fingerprint, workspace, resolved instructions/tool-policy revisions and binding revision, never plaintext secret values. Validate the process row matches the admitted connection/driver/model before attaching an attempt.
   238	5. Otherwise stop/reap/recover the previous process, create a new mark/instance, fsync planned ownership, prepare the explicit environment/launch plan, spawn through org-supervise, fsync PID/start/boot identity, then admit input. No replacement starts while cleanup is unresolved.
   239	6. Journal attempt and turn transitions, pump protocol, persist usage before final completion acknowledgement, release the permit after a verified terminal/idle boundary, and keep the process warm for compatible subsequent turns. Configuration changes do not rewrite the current attempt.
   240	
   241	Each connection is attempted at most once in a dispatch cycle. Exhaustion yields `POOL_EXHAUSTED` with ordered per-connection reasons and any known earliest cooldown time; the turn becomes blocked. Explicit ResumeTurn starts another bounded cycle, not an unbounded retry loop. Concurrent input is BUSY; this version has no implicit scheduling queue.

   243	## 7. Failover, checkpoints and side effects
   244	
   245	Retry-eligible driver errors are rate_limited, quota_exhausted, auth_expired and model_unavailable. Invalid input, policy denial, unsupported capability and unknown protocol/provider errors are not automatic retry instructions. A switching attempt retains usage already consumed, ends/reconciles the old process where required, releases/quarantines its permit and selects the next eligible connection for the same logical turn.
   246	
   247	| Proven execution boundary | Required action |
   248	| --- | --- |
   249	| Before any external/tool effect; adapter proves effect_state none | Replay the frozen turn on the next connection after old-process cleanup. Provisional streamed text is attempt output, not a second committed final reply. |
   250	| Effects occurred; a verified compatible checkpoint includes completed operation receipts and no unknown in-flight effect | Resume after that checkpoint. Do not replay completed tools. |
   251	| Effect state unknown, missing checkpoint/receipt or unsupported cross-driver/account resume | Stop/reconcile and set RECOVERY_REQUIRED. Keep the task/worktree and evidence; do not blindly retry. |
   252	
   253	A checkpoint is an immutable private JSON object with schema_version, checkpoint_id, turn_id, attempt_id, employee_id, workspace_key, input/policy digests, visible message/event watermark, completed tool receipt references, any native conversation-state reference, format_id, portability and content_sha256. Portability is one of same_process, same_connection, same_driver or portable. A destination adapter must explicitly accept that format/version/scope and pass its conformance tests; same vendor/model name is insufficient. Missing context-window capacity returns CONTEXT_LIMIT, not silent truncation. Opaque account-bound CLI state cannot be relabelled portable.
   254	
   255	Every brokered effect has a durable tool receipt `{operation_id, payload_sha256, turn_id, status, result_ref}`. Journal pending before invocation and terminal outcome before acknowledging its result. Same operation/payload returns the recorded outcome; a different payload conflicts. A crash between side effect and receipt completion produces outcome_unknown and requires reconciliation, not an automatic second invocation. Native unbrokered tools need verified start/completion visibility; otherwise the adapter marks effects unknown from the point visibility is lost. Message sends, repository commits and deployment calls are effects too. Pending approvals from an old attempt are cancelled and cannot authorize a replacement.
   256	
   257	Native CLI environments change only on a new process launch. When an API-backed backend ships, its isolated HTTP agent worker owns the common agent loop and exposes a versioned turn/usage/tool protocol; a raw SDK completion is not a complete agent runtime. Supervisor-approved tool requests go through the tool broker. API secrets enter only the approved provider-client context; ordinary tool children do not inherit them. An in-process connection switch is allowed only when the worker advertises verified compatible switching and has no in-flight effect; the supervisor remains the sole switch authority.
   258	
   259	This qualifies source FR-6 deliberately: automatic mid-turn failover is required at a proven safe replay/resume boundary. RECOVERY_REQUIRED is the specified fallback where the harness cannot prove safety, not an unimplemented decision for the team to invent.

   213	| `ResumeTurn` | turn_id, expected_turn_revision; recovery-required turns also require recovery `{checkpoint_ref, receipt_dispositions:[{operation_id, outcome, result_ref, evidence_ref}]}`. Outcome is confirmed_completed or confirmed_not_started, with evidence verified by the tool broker/operator recovery authority. Unknown outcomes remain recovery_required. Retries a blocked turn or resumes only after validated reconciliation. Preserves turn ID, model and workspace. |
   214	| `CancelTurn` | turn_id, expected_turn_revision. Stops current work and becomes cancelled only after completion/cleanup facts are known. |
   215	| `StopAgent` | employee_id, placement_generation. Stops active and idle main processes. It creates no future automatic wake or budget policy. |
   216	| `BindConnection` | connection_id, expected_binding_revision, local credential reference, verified executable path where required. Invalidates observations. Raw credentials use the local auth broker, not this payload. |
   217	| `RefreshConnection` | connection_id. Returns refreshed status/catalog or structured unavailable status. Never starts an employee LLM turn. |
   218	| Queries | GetOperation, GetTurn, GetAgentReadiness, ListProfileModels. Queries have no mutation receipt and expose no secret values. |
   219	
   220	The office validates placement/config revisions and dispatches through the internal supervisor against the same admitted snapshot. No new starts occur while the worker is stopping, recovering or has lost its host-control authority. The existing host/worker launch contract controls that lifecycle; there is no separate server-to-supervisor lease. HQ turn-permit renewal remains mandatory under §6. Unresolved cleanup retains the process/turn slot. Client deadlines of 10 seconds are response deadlines only; they do not prove a command failed or cancel accepted work.
   221	
   222	Run input is a private immutable JSON file containing the resolved employee/role/system instructions, visible messages/attachments by content reference, approved tool/policy manifests, work scope, requested model and ordered pool snapshot. Large content uses content-addressed local references; it is not embedded past the frame limit. Resolve paths against the office's approved roots and reject traversal/symlink substitution. The same turn keeps its original target model, profile order, workspace and input digest through every attempt. Connection disabling, revoked authority and invalid credentials override old eligibility; ordinary profile/prompt changes take effect on the next turn. Resume does not silently broaden the admitted policy.
   316	## 10. Required acceptance criteria
   317	
   318	| ID | Passing evidence |
   319	| --- | --- |
   320	| AE-01 | Person execution config rejected; existing employee IDs/handles/roles/team relationships remain unchanged. |
   321	| AE-02 | Connection registration creates exactly one default pool/member under same-ID retries; generated profile invariants survive restore. |
   322	| AE-03 | Duplicate/out-of-range priorities and cross-organization links fail; reorder is atomic; assigned/used profiles cannot be silently deleted. |
   323	| AE-04 | Two simultaneous RunTurn commands for one employee admit at most one open turn/process; lost ACK replay starts no second child. |
   324	| AE-05 | Isolated bindings select intended accounts; no secrets/global-environment mutation; binding revision invalidates cached readiness. |
   325	| AE-06 | Union is derived; stale/unknown entitlement or unsupported policy does not become runnable; pool order is deterministic. |
   326	| AE-07 | Two offices competing for one configured slot receive at most one active permit; expiry/unresolved cleanup does not free capacity. |
   327	| AE-08 | 429 updates correct quota scope, default cooldown is 900 seconds, attempt count per cycle is bounded by pool size. |
   328	| AE-09 | Pre-effect replay uses the next connection; recorded-effect resume does not repeat a tool; unknown effect enters recovery_required. |
   329	| AE-10 | Crashes before spawn, after spawn before identity acknowledgement, during tools and during supervisor restart all retain evidence and block unsafe replacement. |
   330	| AE-11 | Warm compatible process is reused; changed binding/model/workspace/policy digest causes controlled cleanup/relaunch. |
   331	| AE-12 | Actual successful and failed route usage survives fresh-cache reconstruction; tokens/cost are not assigned to the configured primary when backup consumed them. |
   332	| AE-13 | Cached candidate selection for up to 64 members has p95 below 5 ms over 10,000 warmed lookups on recorded CI hardware. Report quota/network/probe/startup time separately; no performance claim without the result. |
   333	| AE-14 | Every production adapter has pinned-version auth/model/tool/checkpoint/stop/usage fixtures. Unsupported capability returns its defined error, never a permissive fallback. |
   334	| AE-15 | The office worker's supervisor is its single agent recovery owner; host recovery cannot race that live owner. No new placement starts until old ownership is fenced/reconciled. |
   335	| AE-16 | Fresh setup downloads/verifies one complete release, creates HQ only and registers/starts one service. No satellite option is offered; satellite requests are rejected before provisioning. Interrupted/repeated/concurrent setup reuses durable steps and creates no duplicate service, identity or office. HQ-initiated satellite onboarding is a separate flow. |
   336	| AE-17 | Offline HQ setup performs zero external requests, rejects untrusted/incomplete bundles, and never starts satellite enrollment. Missing service-manager support reports foreground instructions; serve starts installed releases without a download prerequisite. |
   337	| AE-18 | Concurrent registration of the same subscription admits one connection/default profile. Disabled/archived duplicates are rejected; distinct subscriptions are accepted. Two office bindings reuse one connection and its quota/cooldown state. Mismatched or unverified binding identity never becomes ready; credential rotation cannot create fresh quota under another connection ID. |
   338	
   339	## 11. Implementation sequence and integration boundaries
   340	
   341	1. Implement versioned application migrations and serializers/projectors from the consolidated schema and this contract (AE-01..03 and subscription identity in AE-18). Preserve employee identity; do not create a second agents table. Document 04 and schema.sql already include these design relationships; applying an application migration is separate implementation work.
   342	2. Add configuration/discovery handlers and typed local credential bindings, using fake driver fixtures first (AE-05..06, AE-18).
   343	3. Implement HQ permit coordinator and office command/receipt journal (AE-04, AE-07..08).
   344	4. Integrate supervisor/router/session-runner modules inside agentic-org-office, host startup/launch admission and the existing recovery adapter (AE-10..11, AE-15). Apply the executable names in §2 with existing signed-launch/credential tests; retain agent-os as the small separate CLI.
   345	5. Implement native adapters and, when its backend ships, the HTTP worker/agent loop behind the same port; gate each production backend on AE-09/14. Unsupported drivers can remain explicitly unavailable while supported backends ship.
   346	6. Connect durable usage capture/routing evidence and restoration (AE-12), then report the performance gate (AE-13).
   347	
   348	The first release accepts explicit turn commands only. Automatic schedules, long-term memory/consolidation, native delegate orchestration and cross-agent messaging policy are not hidden prerequisites; callers submit authorized input to this execution service. Later features use this service rather than creating another process owner. Provider/client libraries and platform launch extensions remain implementation work, but the ownership, state and failure behavior above are fixed.
   349	
   350	## 12. SQL tables, relationships and file mapping
   351	
   352	The tables, view, indexes and triggers below are included in [schema.sql](schema.sql). Load that consolidated draft once; there is no second execution-extension apply step. [Agent structure](04-agent-structure.md) owns the agent_placements table and its placement_generation column. These triggers reject generation regression, office moves without an increment and changing a configured agent into a person. HQ still verifies cleanup/fencing; a SQL generation check alone cannot prove an old process stopped. Use schema-versioned application migrations and rebuild projections from the authorities in §3. Common attribution follows [record contracts](08-record-contracts.md); missing legacy metadata is not fabricated.

   132	- A runnable agent has one execution configuration selecting one pool and one target model. People have no execution configuration; an agent without one is not runnable.
   133	- A valid pool contains 1–64 distinct connection IDs in contiguous priority order. Many agents can select one pool, and one connection can be reused by several pools. Array order becomes priorities 1, 2, 3, and so on.
   134	- Connection creation atomically creates one generated single-connection default profile. Manually assembled pools coexist with those defaults. Converting a default into a manual pool clears its generated designation; it cannot keep claiming to be that connection's generated default.
   135	- Two connection IDs cannot represent the same `(organization_id, provider_type, subscription_identity)`, even if one is disabled/archived. Two offices using one subscription create two local bindings to the same connection. A subscription pool's different connections represent different subscriptions.
   136	- Each office has at most one binding per connection. Credentials/CLI auth state stay private to the office or credential vault. The shared connection record never contains secrets or office-specific credential paths.
   137	- A connection can expose many models; the same canonical model can be available through multiple connections. A pool's model list is the union of discovered confirmed support. Connections need not expose identical catalogs; only those supporting the agent's chosen model can serve its turn.
   138	- Pool failover preserves the chosen canonical model. Changing models is a separate configuration decision, not an implicit consequence of selecting another connection.
   139	- Quota/cooldown admission belongs to the organization-wide connection and is shared across its pools, agents and office bindings. API/cloud provider-wide quota grouping is not inferred from different API keys; document 11 explicitly limits the subscription-identity rule to verified subscription contexts.
   140	
   141	The pool's minimum size, contiguous priorities, generated-profile contents, registry validation, fresh model eligibility and quota capacity are service transaction/readiness rules. SQL enforces the scoped foreign keys, distinct membership/priority, generated-default uniqueness and subscription identity/replacement constraints. SQL alone cannot prove external subscription identity or available quota.

# S0: Codex app-server

Status: **in progress**. This checkpoint verifies the local protocol and standalone
sandboxed commands. It does not complete S0 or verify a model-driven tool turn.
The brief is ada's `docs/design/agent-sessions.md` on `ada/agent-sessions`, with
the source research in `docs/research/agent-runtimes-control.md`.

## Run the offline probe

Tested on macOS 26.7.2 arm64, Codex CLI **0.167.0**, Node 26.13.0.
Pass the real absolute Codex binary path:

```sh
node spikes/codex/probe.mjs /absolute/path/to/codex
CODEX_S0_OUTPUT=/private/tmp/codex-s0.json node spikes/codex/probe.mjs /absolute/path/to/codex
# Skip the unchanged Git checks while iterating on sockets/profiles:
node spikes/codex/probe.mjs /absolute/path/to/codex --socket-only
```

The probe creates and removes a private directory under `/private/tmp`. Only its
child processes receive a temporary `HOME` and `CODEX_HOME`. They have no sign-in,
MCP configuration, installed plugins, API keys, or real organization data. The
session token is a synthetic fixture. It never sends `turn/start` and never calls
a model. The optional artifact contains sanitized JSON-RPC frames and stderr;
temporary root paths become `<TMP>`. It is written with mode 0600 on creation.

`/usr/bin/git` is an Xcode launcher on this Mac. Resolve Git with `xcrun --find git`
before sandboxing. The launcher stalled inside the sandbox; the resolved binary
committed successfully. The probe does this resolution automatically.

## Verified locally

| Check | Result / boundary |
| --- | --- |
| One `codex app-server --stdio` child, JSONL `initialize`/`initialized` | Works without authentication. |
| `command/exec`, `sandboxPolicy.type=workspaceWrite` | A workspace write succeeds; a write outside the explicit roots fails with `Operation not permitted`. |
| Session environment | The synthetic `ORG_SESSION_TOKEN` and `ORG_AGENT` survive the pinned shell environment settings in **standalone command/exec**. This does not prove model tool behavior or `msg.bind`. |
| Task worktree commit | Works with workspace, scratch, objects/refs/logs and literal own-admin paths. The admin folder's `gitdir` and `commondir` are excluded. |
| Shared Git files | Writes to `work.git/config`, `hooks/probe`, `HEAD`, `info/exclude` and the worktree's `commondir`/`gitdir` are refused. |
| Git config | `extensions.worktreeConfig=true`; bare setting moved to `config.worktree`. A task's `git config --worktree` succeeds. `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` pins an empty hooks path, fsmonitor off, automatic GC/maintenance off, and commitGraph off. Global config is a generated fixture containing only commit identity. |
| Harmless Git diagnostic | `packed-refs.lock` is outside the task roots. Git printed a lock refusal, exited 0 and produced the expected commit. |
| Default Unix socket access | Legacy `workspaceWrite`, network off: fixture office connection fails with `EPERM`. |
| Explicit Unix socket allowlist | A named permissions profile plus `features.network_proxy=true` permits exactly the listed fixture socket. An unlisted socket and a separate direct TCP loopback listener both fail with `EPERM`. |
| Profile file carveout | A file inside the writable workspace marked `deny` cannot be read or overwritten. The original synthetic contents remain intact. |
| Profile thread startup | `thread/start` accepts `permissions`, `developerInstructions`, `approvalPolicy=on-request` and `approvalsReviewer=user` without a model call. |
| Empty thread resume | A fresh process rejects resume of a never-used thread with `no rollout found`. Resume after a real turn is still open. |

The environment pins exercised are:

```text
shell_environment_policy.inherit="all"
shell_environment_policy.ignore_default_excludes=true
shell_environment_policy.include_only=["PATH","HOME","TMPDIR","SHELL","LANG","ORG_AGENT","ORG_SESSION_TOKEN","GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM","GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL"]
```

This is the fixture list, not the final office list. The office must include its
other allowed environment names, including the indexed `GIT_CONFIG_*` names.
The default standalone `command/exec` also retained the fixture token here; don't
use that as evidence that model shell tools retain it without the pins.

## Exact sandbox fields

Schemas generated by the installed 0.167.0 binary establish:

- `thread/start`: `developerInstructions`, `config`, and either `sandbox` (an enum)
  or `permissions` (a named profile). There is no top-level `writableRoots`.
- `turn/start`: `sandboxPolicy.type="workspaceWrite"` with `writableRoots`, or
  `permissions` for a named profile. The schema says they cannot be combined.
- `thread/resume` accepts `developerInstructions` and `permissions` too.
- Legacy workspaceWrite has no deny-read or subtractive write-deny field. Its
  objects/info limitation requires the design's fallback when that policy is used.
  Named profiles can express a file deny, as verified above. The full Git and
  office deny lists under a profile are not yet verified.

The working socket profile overrides are equivalent to this TOML:

```toml
[features]
network_proxy = true

[permissions.office_probe]
extends = ":workspace"

[permissions.office_probe.network]
enabled = true
proxy_url = "http://127.0.0.1:0"
enable_socks5 = false

[permissions.office_probe.network.unix_sockets]
"/absolute/fixture/office.sock" = "allow"
```

`command/exec` selects it with `permissionProfile: "office_probe"`; threads select
it with `permissions: "office_probe"`. With no domain allow entries, the proxy
does not grant external destinations. Only local fixture destinations were probed.
This prototype extends `:workspace`, including its temporary-directory defaults;
the final office profile still needs explicit scratch roots and the full deny list.

Pass the **whole permissions table in one `-c` argument**. The installed CLI's
dotted override parser splits a period in a quoted socket filename into another
key. `features.network_proxy.enabled=true` is also rejected on this version;
`features.network_proxy=true` is the working form. No real config was changed.

Claude 2.1.311's default set has no separate `Glob` or `Grep`; they appeared in `init.tools` when listed (and under `--restricted` alone), so listing them is harmless.
165:     - **Tool search is off.** `ToolSearch` is disallowed, so the office's MCP tools must never be deferred behind it: an office-set switch turns tool search off (`ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=false`). S1 checks that the office's MCP tools appear in `init.tools` and can be called. Fallback: a Claude agent that needs an office MCP tool isn't office-run until they can.
168:     - **Remote control stays off** (rev 3.4): Claude's `initialize` reports `remote_control_available: true` in every run. The adapter never sends a request that turns remote control on, and the start fails if the session reports remote control as active. S0 finds the setting or environment variable that turns it off, and the office sets it.
171:     - Bash's own background mode (`run_in_background`) is turned off with an office-set switch, `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1`, which S1 verifies (see "S0 checks and fallbacks").
172:     - Codex and Antigravity get the same rule where they have such tools: S0 lists each runtime's built-in tools (Codex's web search, say), and the adapter pins its allowlist the runtime's way. Fallback: a runtime whose risky built-in tools can't be turned off isn't office-run.
173:   - **Auth stays in each runtime's own store.** The office never puts API keys in an agent's environment. API-key support, when it's added, goes through each runtime's own credential mechanism.
180:   - **Escalating approvals (contract review of `org-runtime`, 2026-11-08):** every approval request carries a required `escalation`: `none`, `sandbox_bypass` (e.g. a Codex command asking to run unsandboxed), `permission_change` (Claude `ExitPlanMode`, an ACP mode switch) or `unknown`. The office ALWAYS DENIES `sandbox_bypass`: the fixed denies win, with no policy or owner override in phase 1. It NEVER answers `permission_change` or `unknown` from policy: they always go to the owner in Needs you with a clear warning (a request for a disallowed tool is denied at once instead; see Claude's mapping below). Adapters must set the field; an unrecognised approval kind is `unknown`.
186:   - **The office owns expiry.** Claude didn't time out an approval within 150 s in the spike, so the office answers an expired one with a deny. Longer is untested: S1 leaves one unanswered for 31 minutes or more. If the CLI turns out to time out first, the office's expiry is set below the CLI's limit, and a CLI-side timeout is handled like a withdrawal (`cancelled`), so the two never race (see "S0 checks and fallbacks").
188:   - **Policy scopes:** a rule is a tool plus one of: a path pattern, a command prefix (for shell tools), or an MCP server.
193:   - **The fixed denies (under "Security") override every allow rule**, `allow_always` included.
194:   - **No absolute allow rule reaches managed state (rev 3.6).** `permission_policy.set` and `approval.answer` refuse any absolute path pattern whose normalized literal prefix could match the selected instance root, any registered peer instance root, the instance registry, credential paths, release payloads or private runtime directories listed under "Standalone-v1 managed state and grants" (`invalid_request`, reason `managed_state`). Expand `~`, reject `..` components, and resolve the longest existing prefix before testing both ancestor and descendant overlap, so a symlink or `/**` cannot bypass the rule. Workspace-relative rules (`./…`) may cover only the session's own workspace; their real-path targets are checked on every request, fixed denies still win, and they never become native file-write allow rules. The adapter emits the runtime's explicit absolute/relative syntax. No rule grants a whole instance or shared employee-home parent.
195:   - **No write under managed state outside the writable roots, even when allowed once.** The file tools run in the unsandboxed CLI, so the office checks every write request itself (a Claude `can_use_tool` for `Edit` or `Write`, a Codex or ACP file-change approval): if the path, resolved to its real path, is under managed state and outside the session's writable roots, the office denies it at once, without asking, and `allow_once` can't override it. So other projects' `work.git`, an office created mid-session and every other unnamed path there stay read-only. This check sees only requests that reach the office, so **every file write must reach it**: the office never writes an allow rule for a file-writing tool (`Edit`, `Write`) into a runtime's own rules, and headless Claude never runs in `acceptEdits` mode (the spec's `permission_mode` for Claude can only be `default` or `manual`; `acceptEdits`, `auto` and the bypass modes fail to decode). So a write through a symlink the agent planted in its worktree is checked at its real path, whatever the policy allows. Policy rules for those tools are applied by the office when it answers, against the request's **real path**: a path rule allows a write only if the real path matches it. A write whose literal path matches but whose real path doesn't (a planted symlink to `~/Documents/…` or another repository, say) goes to the owner in Needs you. This holds for headless Claude, with one gap: the office resolves the real path when it answers, and the unsandboxed CLI writes afterwards, so a detached tool process could swap a path for a symlink in between (a known limit under "Security"). Codex raises no approval for a write inside its writable roots, so for Codex it's the sandbox's own real-path enforcement that holds (an S0 Codex check). The same check covers siblings of `office-state/`, external credential/runtime paths and peer instance roots. As a second line, this office's other projects' `work.git/` and `worktrees/` are also named write denies at start (`start_denies`), and the runtime's own rules are checked as above. S1 checks that `Edit` and `Write` through a planted symlink are refused, either by Claude's own deny rule or by the office at `can_use_tool`, and records which, and that one to a target outside every deny (`~/Documents/…`) reaches `can_use_tool` and goes to Needs you. Fallback: Claude isn't office-run until they are. Inside managed state, only the writable roots and the reads the fixed denies leave open are reachable (see "Security").

253:  - **Paths are UTF-8 by type.** Every path is a `SpecPath`: absolute, normalized (no `.`, `..` or empty parts, no trailing `/` except `/` itself). It refuses every Cc control (NUL, line breaks, tab, ESC, DEL, C1), U+2028 and U+2029, and every Cf format character as of Unicode 17.0 (bidi controls, zero-width characters and joiners, the soft hyphen, invisible operators, number marks, tags; 170 code points, pinned by a test). `PathPattern` and `CommandPrefix` use the same set. The crate is the exact reference. Patterns, names and tokens are validated types too, so none of them can break out of the argv, file or rule it's written into. 466:### Legacy `work.git` security evidence (revisions 3.3–3.7)
478:- **Explicit `denyWrite` entries, for every runtime** (rev 3.3). Being outside the writable roots isn't enough: Claude's sandbox adds the git common dir by itself (below), and a release could change what it opens, while versions only warn. So every runtime's sandbox and permission policy get a `denyWrite` (a fixed deny) for `work.git/config`, `work.git/config.worktree`, `work.git/hooks/`, `work.git/worktrees/*/config.worktree`, `work.git/objects/info/`, `work.git/HEAD`, `packed-refs`, `info/`, `description`, `FETCH_HEAD`, each worktree's `commondir` and `gitdir` (`work.git/worktrees/*/commondir`, `…/gitdir`), and the admin folders of the other worktrees that exist at start (`work.git/worktrees/<other id>/`, named). The entries other than the named admin folders are wildcarded over every project's `work.git` (`<office home>/offices/*/workspace/projects/*/work.git/config` and so on), not only the session's own project's. None of them is an ancestor of a writable root. S1 asserts each one under Claude's sandbox, and S6 for every runtime. A filter or diff driver planted in `work.git/config` would run in other agents' sessions and in the office's own fetch (which runs in `work.git`, `projects-git-github.md`), so these never depend on a runtime's defaults.
481:- **The office sets the config that matters through the environment** (decision 6): `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`, `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`, and, through `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`/`KEY_n`/`VALUE_n` (which override every config file), the commit identity (from `projects-git-github.md`), an empty `credential.helper`, `core.hooksPath=/dev/null`, `core.fsmonitor=false`, `gc.auto=0` and `maintenance.auto=false`. Without the last two, an automatic gc would try to write outside the writable roots.
483:- **The office's own git near a worktree.** In `work.git/worktrees/<id>/`, the `commondir` and `gitdir` files are read-only to agents (left out of the writable roots). Before any office git command touches a worktree (`worktree remove`, re-creating one, the check for uncommitted work), the office deletes that worktree's `config.worktree` and rewrites `commondir` and `gitdir` to their known values. Agents can't write the worktree's own `.git` file (a fixed deny), but as a second line of defence the office also deletes it (file, folder or symlink) and writes it again with its known value, and it never lets git discover the repository through it: it sets `GIT_DIR=work.git/worktrees/<id>` and `GIT_WORK_TREE=<the worktree>` explicitly. (`git worktree remove` checks that file, so rewriting it also keeps removal from getting stuck.) Then it runs with its hardening (`projects-git-github.md`): no global or system config and hooks off. So no filter driver, hook or redirected repository that an agent planted can run in the office's git.
487:- **Home sessions in a git repository.** An agent's home is often a folder inside a repository (ours are in the agents repository), and the agent commits its memory and journal there. It can't be the repository's root (see "Security"). Its writable roots then also include, in that repository's `.git/`, only what a commit needs: `objects/` (except `objects/info/`), `refs/` and `logs/`, plus these files by their literal paths (they may not exist yet): `index`, `index.lock`, `HEAD`, `HEAD.lock`, `ORIG_HEAD`, `COMMIT_EDITMSG`, `packed-refs`, `packed-refs.lock`, `AUTO_MERGE` and `AUTO_MERGE.lock`. (Without the last two, a commit works with a harmless lock error.) Everything else in `.git/` stays read-only, including `config`, `hooks/`, `info/`, `commondir`, `worktrees/` and `modules/`. With the fixed deny on writing any `.git` entry inside the workspace (under "Security"), an agent can't point git at a config it wrote. The same environment applies, so that repository's own hooks don't run in office-run sessions.
488:  - S0 checks that each sandbox can allow a literal path that doesn't exist yet. Claude's can (verified: the commit worked with several of them missing). If one can't, it keeps `config`, `hooks/`, `info/` and `objects/info/` denied and also denies `commondir`, `worktrees/`, `modules/`, `config.worktree`, `rebase-merge/`, `rebase-apply/` and `sequencer/`.
490:- **Tests:** S0 checks that `git commit` works inside each runtime's sandbox with these roots, for a task worktree and for a home inside a repository, and notes any harmless lock errors (a commit can try `work.git/packed-refs.lock`). Done for Claude: a task commit works with `work.git/HEAD`, `packed-refs`, `info/`, `description`, `FETCH_HEAD` and `gitdir` denied (one run), and with `objects/info/`, `commondir` and `gitdir` denied (another run); the combined list wasn't run, so S1 runs it. A home commit works with the design's roots; the office's git environment applies inside the sandbox (the run with the full deny list didn't pass that environment). **The spike's commits ran in its own layout under `/tmp`, not under `<office home>`**, so S1 commits from a task worktree at its real path (`<office dir>/workspace/projects/<project id>/worktrees/<task id>/`), with the full deny table under "Security" in force and the rev 3.3 git environment (`GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`, `core.hooksPath=/dev/null`). The spike probed only listed paths in `work.git` and only the agent's own worktree folder, so S1 enumerates every path in `work.git` under Claude's sandbox (other worktrees' folders, `shallow`, `modules/`, lock files, …) and builds the `denyWrite` list from that. Until then, more of `work.git` may be writable than this section says. S6 checks that a hostile `work.git` config or hook planted by agent A doesn't run in agent B, and that a hostile `config.worktree` with a `.gitattributes` filter, or a worktree `.git` file pointed at a planted repository, doesn't run anything during the office's worktree removal or re-creation, and that removal and re-creation still succeed. And when a home session tries to write `.git/commondir`, `.git/worktrees/*/commondir` or a new `<home>/.git`, those writes are denied, and the user's `git status` runs nothing.

539:- **The workspace is hostile.** An agent can write anything in its worktree, so nothing there may change a session's **settings, permissions, hooks, tools or MCP servers**:
550:  - **Every runtime must hold the read denies** (rev 3.3). They now cover more than encrypted databases and sockets (other organizations' offices, every agent's runtime dir, `~/.claude/**`, the Keychain files), so a runtime whose sandbox can't deny reads isn't office-run. Per S0 Codex, Codex's legacy `sandboxPolicy` can't, and a permissions profile can (a file deny was verified; the full lists are still to verify). S0 checks Antigravity.
551:  - writes to the **user's own config**, which runtimes and the user's tools load: `~/.claude/**`, `~/.claude.json` (the user's and local MCP servers), `~/.codex/**`, `~/.gemini/**`, `~/.agents/**`, `~/.config/gh/**`, `~/.gitconfig`, `~/.config/git/**`, `~/.ssh/**`, the shell start-up files (`~/.zshenv`, `~/.zprofile`, `~/.zshrc`, `~/.bash_profile`, `~/.bashrc`, `~/.profile`; `PATH` is captured from them), and `~/Library/LaunchAgents/**`. The runtimes write their own stores there themselves; this denies it to the agent's tools. The sandboxes' writable roots leave them out too.
552:  - **reads of `~/.claude/**` and `~/.claude.json`** by the agent's tools. `~/.claude.json` holds the user's MCP server configs (which can carry tokens) and per-project history. Office-run Claude agents use the user's real `~/.claude` (decision 6), so it holds every agent's transcripts and the user's own, and the user's settings and history. The Claude CLI itself isn't sandboxed and still reads it; its tools can't (the sandbox holds Bash, the policy's deny rule holds the file tools). A runtime whose sandbox can't deny these reads isn't office-run (above).
553:  - **`/tmp/cc-socks/**`** and **`/private/tmp/cc-socks/**`** (macOS's `/tmp` is a symlink, and the spike tested only the real path), reads, writes and connections. Each Claude process listens on `/tmp/cc-socks/<pid>.sock`, a fixed, machine-wide folder shared with the user's own interactive sessions, so the session's `TMPDIR` doesn't cover it. With `allowUnixSockets` listing only the office socket, an agent's tools can't connect to any of them, its own Claude's included. What a holder of a messaging token could do over such a socket wasn't tested, so no exception is made.
555:  - **reads of the user's Keychain files** (`~/Library/Keychains/**`) by the agent's tools, so a tool can't read the runtimes' sign-ins (Claude's `Claude Code-credentials` item) or anything else of the user's there. A Keychain item can also be read through the system's security service rather than the file, so this deny alone may not hold: S1 tests `security find-generic-password -s "Claude Code-credentials" -w` from a tool, and Claude isn't office-run until it fails without asking the user anything (see "S0 checks and fallbacks").
556:- **Known limit, Claude take-over** (rev 3.3): in a take-over, `claude --resume` runs as the interactive TUI, and its permission prompts go to the person, not to `can_use_tool`. So the office's own write check (decision 7) doesn't run, and the person can switch to `acceptEdits` (or `auto`), which allows edits, through a symlink an agent planted too, without a prompt. The fixed and named denies still apply as Claude's deny rules. Whether those rules match a symlink's real path is isolated by an S1 check ("S0 checks and fallbacks"); if they match only literal paths, the take-over warning says so. A person is at the keyboard, so we accept it, and the app says so when a person takes over a Claude agent. S1 checks whether a Claude settings key can lock `acceptEdits` and `auto` out of the TUI; if one can, the office's settings set it.
557:- **Known limit, a symlink swapped after an answer** (rev 3.3): the office checks a file write's real path when it answers the request, and Claude's unsandboxed CLI writes afterwards. A detached tool process can replace a workspace path with a symlink in that window, and the write then lands wherever the symlink points, unless one of Claude's own deny rules matches it. S1 checks whether Claude's `Edit` and `Write` re-check deny rules at write time or refuse to follow symlinks. If they refuse to follow symlinks, this closes. If they only re-check deny rules at write time (and those rules match real paths, the S1 run under "S0 checks and fallbacks"), the gap narrows to targets no deny rule names. Real isolation (an OS sandbox around the CLI) is v2.
558:- **Known limit, Codex take-over:** a person in Codex's TUI can switch its sandbox or approval policy from inside (`/approvals`), which also lifts the fixed denies for that take-over. A person is at the keyboard, so we accept it, the office pins both again when it resumes headless, and the app says so when a person takes over a Codex agent. S0 tries Codex's managed requirements (`allowed_sandbox_modes`, `allowed_approval_policies`) to lock `danger-full-access` out.
559:- **Antigravity** is gated: S4 doesn't ship until the spike proves that agy's runtime dir and `.agents/` (the agent file, `hooks.json` and rules, including those that arrive through a git checkout) can't be written by the agent, or aren't loaded. Otherwise Antigravity ships with that as a documented, accepted limit, and the app tells the owner when they enable an Antigravity agent. That limit covers only `.agents/` content that arrives in the workspace, never the fixed denies: Antigravity doesn't ship until its sandbox holds the runtime-dir denies and the read denies, like every runtime.

1	# Design: agent sessions (the office runs the agents)
     2	
     3	Status: **selected execution integration requirements, rev 4** (2026-11-15).
     4	Documentation only: the complete runner, pool routing and production composition
     5	are not implemented by this design. [Execution](organization-data/11-model-profiles-and-agent-execution.md)
     6	owns the selected turn/process contract; [employees](organization-data/04-agent-structure.md),
     7	[connections/pools](organization-data/14-model-providers-and-connection-pools.md),
     8	[recovery](organization-data/16-recovery-and-office-continuity.md) and
     9	[budgets](organization-data/17-budgets-and-controls.md) own their respective data.
    10	Use the [authority map](documentation-authority.md) for precedence.
    11	
    12	This document retains the runtime research, adapter restrictions and security
    13	validation from revisions 3.2–3.7. Exact `work.git`, instance-home, API v1 and native
    14	CLI examples are labeled compatibility evidence where retained. They are not a
    15	second target layout or a claim of implemented launches. The earlier complete
    16	proposal is available in [the pre-reconciliation revision](https://github.com/vgmello/agentic-org/blob/c6e520a36c4dc7c738c68915fac5e7d5d1cbe804/docs/design/agent-sessions.md).
    17	Research fixtures are in [agent runtimes control](../research/agent-runtimes-control.md).
    18	
    19	Current executable/source names are agentic-org, agentic-org-office,
    20	agentic-org-web and agent-os; org-host is a library. See
    21	[executable migration](executable-migration.md) for available entry points.
    22	The browser does not own process lifetime. Human controls use authenticated HQ
    23	operations and the placed office; interactive takeover requires an authorized
    24	local CLI operation until a separate browser-terminal contract is approved.
    25	The macOS Keychain/sandbox evidence below does not establish Linux adapter readiness.
    26	
    27	### Managed home contract (standalone v1)
    28	
    29	The following is the earlier standalone v2 managed-home/retired-field proposal,
    30	not the selected task tree or a claim that transport v2 has shipped. The selected
    31	launcher still rejects arbitrary caller-set paths and resolves approved workspace
    32	keys; any legacy home metadata is provenance only. Preserve versioned callers and
    33	security checks while the target mapping is implemented.
    34	
    35	Resolve every home launch from the configured instance root and stable office/member
    36	IDs. Preflight validates the actual resolved path and filesystem identity against
    37	the fixed denies; stale profile metadata, symlinks and caller input cannot redirect
    38	it. (amended 2026-11-10: X-02 D7) The managed home leaves `AgentProfile`: the owning
    39	office reports this effective path as status, with its office and freshness (X-02 §8,
    40	`who`'s `managed_home`; an approved draft not yet in this repo, see the launch v3 note
    41	in office-host-boundary.md §3), so PROF-4 displays the same home the launcher uses.
    42	
    43	Retire `member.update_agent`'s caller-settable `home` and `clear_home`, and refuse
    44	home overrides in all create/update inputs before filesystem access. The first
    45	standalone local protocol is API_VERSION 2 under ADR-0001; remove/update affected
    46	callers and fixtures together. Historical or imported profile paths are provenance
    47	only, never launch authority. Test forged absolute paths, traversal, `clear_home`,
    48	stale placement, and symlink redirection without creating an external directory.
    49	
    50	## Decisions
    51	1. **Headless-first.** The office drives every agent as a child process over the runtime's structured JSON-lines protocol:
    52	   - **Claude Code:** `claude -p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --verbose`, one long-lived process per session.
    53	   - **Codex:** `codex app-server` over **stdio**, one process per session, with one thread in it. There's no socket. A shared app-server waits until a spike proves that its threads are isolated from each other and from agents.
    54	   - **Antigravity:** `agy acp` (the Agent Client Protocol). `agy` stream-json is the fallback only if the spike shows ACP isn't ready, and then approvals follow decision 7's fallback.
    55	
    56	   **This replaces the `--bg` + `claude attach` choice** of the unmerged ADR-0004 draft (`0004-session-panel-embedded-terminal`), which spike S2 confirmed. `--bg` has no programmatic prompt channel, no structured events and no usage stream, and the office needs all three. A person can still work with an agent directly (see "Taking over"). ADR-0004 is rewritten to match before it merges, once the user agrees (U-S4).
    57	2. **One port, one adapter per runtime, one supervisor.**
    58	   - `org-runtime` is the **port**: `AgentRuntime`, an optional `RuntimeHost`, `Session`, `SessionSpec`, `LaunchContext`, `LaunchPlan`, the normalized `SessionEvent`, `Capabilities`, usage types, and the one line framer and encoder that every adapter and the pump share. It's a contract, like `org-proto`. It does no I/O.
    59	     - `AgentRuntime` is a stateless factory per runtime: its capabilities, the launch plan and the `Session` for a session (from a `SessionSpec` and a `LaunchContext`), and the launch plans for its **probes** (preflight, and the usage poll where a runtime needs one) with the parsing of their output.
    60	     - `RuntimeHost` is a shared host process that serves several sessions. It's optional and deferred: River's first version leaves it out, and it's added, additively, when a runtime shares a process. Nothing uses it while Codex runs one app-server per session.
    61	     - `Session` is **sans-I/O**: a pure state machine for one runtime's protocol. The pump tells it what happened (`start`, `on_line`, `on_truncated`, `on_stderr_line`, `on_stdout_closed`, `on_exit`, `on_tick(now)`, and `control` for an office command), and it returns outputs in order: `Write` (one line for stdin), `Event` (for the office), `CloseStdin` or `Abort` (stop the process now: the pump runs the fast stop under "Processes and safety"; rev 3.3, for a failed `init` check of tools, plugins or MCP servers). It never spawns, reads, writes, sleeps or reads the clock (time is an input), so it's tested from recorded fixtures alone. Its contract is under "The model".
    62	   - The port is **synchronous**, with no async runtime.
    63	   - Planned adapters `org-runtime-claude`, `org-runtime-codex` and `org-runtime-agy` will implement it; none of those crates exists in this checkout. Runtime research/spike fixtures are separate evidence, not implemented adapters. An adapter **builds a launch plan** (argv, env additions, files to write) and a `Session` for its protocol. It never spawns and never touches a pipe.
    64	   - `org-supervise` is the **one place that spawns agent runtimes** and their probes. Piped children are implemented; PTYs for takeover remain separate work. It owns process control only: process groups, the env allowlist, the stop sequence, reaping and orphan cleanup. It speaks no runtime protocol. It's also the single spawn path for every other process the host or a server starts (`org-git`'s git, the host's office servers), as `office-host-boundary.md` §4 says (as amended on `ada/docs-followups-3`); only the agent-runtime parts (the env allowlist, marks, the stop plan) are specific to agents.
    65	   - **The lock** on an agent is released only after verified owned-process/descendant cleanup and reaping; a process exit or thread unload alone cannot establish that proof.
    66	   - Adapters depend only on `org-runtime`: never on each other, on `org-supervise`, on `org-office` or on storage.
    67	   - **`org-office` depends on neither `org-runtime` nor `org-supervise`.** It holds admitted execution rules as domain logic (turn state, limits and history; automatic queues remain deferred) and defines the small trait it needs to act on sessions, in its own terms (`SessionControl`: start, send, interrupt and stop a session by id, and **probe** a runtime for preflight or usage). The planned integration library **`org-office-sessions`** implements it with `org-supervise` and the adapters, maps the office's session record to a `SessionSpec` and a `LaunchContext`, and runs the **pump**, one implementation for every runtime. For each live session it owns the child's pipes, splits stdout and stderr with the port's framer, feeds each line to the `Session`, applies its outputs in order, calls `on_tick` at the session's next deadline, and feeds the facts (turn ended, approval requested, usage, exit) into `org-office`. It also implements `SessionAuth` (see "Messaging"). `agentic-org-office`, the composition root, wires it in. See "Where the code lives".
    68	   - The volatile third-party CLIs sit behind a stable port, so a runtime's protocol change touches one adapter.
    69	3. **Durable facts, disposable projections.** Organization Git owns employee and
    70	   execution definitions. Protected execution journals own turn/attempt/process
    71	   transitions, immutable inputs, tool receipts, checkpoints and command outcomes;
    72	   HQ's protected journal owns placement generations, permits and cooldowns.
    73	   SQLite indexes these sources. A bounded event log or runtime transcript alone
    74	   cannot establish whether an effect completed. Transcript plaintext behavior in
    75	   the earlier native CLI spike is a platform/privacy limitation to disclose and
    76	   validate, not permission to put prompts into ordinary logs or organization Git.
    77	4. **Identity, placement and workspaces are separate.** Every employee has one
    78	   required home team and optional role/reporting line in `profile.md`; only an
    79	   agent can have `execution.md`, selecting one pool and canonical model. A person
    80	   has no execution process. The owner security principal is not an execution
    81	   employee; representing the owner/HR as an employee still requires a home team.
    82	   Placement may change independently of identity, subject to fencing.
    83	
    84	   The selected runtime paths are:
    85	
    86	   ```text
    87	   runtime/<office-id>/
    88	   ├── repositories/<repository-id>.git/        # one office cache per registered repo
    89	   └── teams/<root-team-id>/teams/<child-team-id>/.../agents/<employee-id>/
    90	       ├── projects/<project-id>/tasks/<task-id>/repositories/<repository-id>/
    91	       └── tasks/<task-id>/repositories/<repository-id>/  # projectless team task
    92	   ```
    93	
    94	   A project can use several registered repositories; each association requires
    95	   its own integration branch. Workspace records bind office, employee, task and
    96	   repository; a session's cwd is an approved workspace reference, never arbitrary
    97	   caller input. A non-task turn uses an explicitly approved workspace key; this
    98	   does not select automatic home sessions or a memory engine.
    99	   One open logical turn and one not-gone main process slot exist per employee.
   100	   No native delegate/helper exception is selected. Handoff, process exit and turn
   101	   completion are not task closure: preserve task worktrees and unpushed work.
   102	   A missing workspace is a recovery issue; restore only from verified repository
   103	   and retained task state, disclosing any unpushed loss rather than assuming a
   104	   pushed branch contains everything.
   105	5. **The admitted launch restrictions are replayed on every start and resume.** The adapter-specific mappings below are compatibility requirements; document 11 freezes input, pool/model, workspace and policy per logical turn. A changed next-turn launch digest requires controlled cleanup/relaunch rather than changing a live child. Claude's `--resume` doesn't restore `--settings`, `--mcp-config`, `--plugin-dir` or `--add-dir`, a `-p` resume starts in Manual permission mode, Codex filters threads by cwd, and Antigravity's conversations are tied to the cwd. So the office stores the whole spec and always replays it, in the session's own workspace.
   106	   - The spec includes the permission mode and the sandbox mode. Claude always gets `--permission-mode`. Codex gets `approvalPolicy`, `approvalsReviewer: "user"` and `permissions` (the session's named profile) on every `thread/start`, `thread/resume` and `turn/start`, and never the legacy `sandbox` or `sandboxPolicy`, which would override the profile (per S0 Codex, live turns still to verify).
   107	   - `spec_hash` covers the whole spec. The conversation to resume isn't part of the spec (it's in the `LaunchContext`), so a resume hashes the same as the first start. Claude keeps the system prompt it recorded at the first request (`--system-prompt-snapshot`), so when a resume's `spec_hash` differs and the stored instructions differ from the new ones (the hash also changes with the policy's version), the office sends the change as a message ("Your instructions changed: …").
   108	   - **The Claude spike confirmed it:** `--resume` works from any cwd, even after the original cwd was deleted. The system prompt (the agent's prompt and the appended file) is snapshotted, and `--settings` isn't restored, so a resume without it asks for approvals the settings allowed.
   109	   - **Bypass modes are banned everywhere**, headless and interactive:
   110	     - Claude: `bypassPermissions` and `--dangerously-skip-permissions`. The office's settings set `disableBypassPermissionsMode: "disable"`, so the take-over TUI can't switch to it either.
   111	     - Codex: `danger-full-access`, `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` (and its `--yolo` alias in releases that have it), and `--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust`. The take-over TUI gets the same `-c` pins as the app-server, but a person can still change them from inside it (a known limit under "Security", unless S0 can lock them).
   112	     - Antigravity: `--dangerously-skip-permissions`.
   113	6. **Isolation by default.** The exact instance/temp/`work.git`/native-auth
   114	   mappings below are the earlier adapter restrictions (revisions 3.3–3.7), retained
