Employee-owned delegate tools may be added only after the registration, permission, budget and cancellation checks in [`employee-supervision.md` §6](employee-supervision.md#6-capability-checks-implementation-slices-and-validation) pass for the installed runtime. This is a narrow capability extension, never general background or cross-session access. Every `init` is checked against the resulting verified list.
   164	     - **The baseline allowlist** is `Read`, `Edit`, `Write`, `Glob`, `Grep`, `Bash` (sandboxed) and the office-provided MCP tools (`mcp__<office server>__<tool>`), and nothing else. It's the spec's required `tools` (see "The model"). The adapter passes its built-in names as `--tools` (in the spike, a non-empty `--tools` list ran only with `--restricted`, and gave `init.tools` exactly the listed tools, where `--restricted` alone left 24; `--tools ""` alone removed every built-in tool; a non-empty list alone is for S1 to confirm; `--tools ""` didn't hide MCP tools, and MCP names in `--tools` are untested), and the whole list, MCP names included, as the inline agent's `tools` (which also restricted the main thread's tools in the spike). Claude 2.1.311's default set has no separate `Glob` or `Grep`; they appeared in `init.tools` when listed (and under `--restricted` alone), so listing them is harmless.
   165	     - **Tool search is off.** `ToolSearch` is disallowed, so the office's MCP tools must never be deferred behind it: an office-set switch turns tool search off (`ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=false`). S1 checks that the office's MCP tools appear in `init.tools` and can be called. Fallback: a Claude agent that needs an office MCP tool isn't office-run until they can.
   166	     - **The disallowed list:** `--disallowedTools` names every other tool in the spike's recorded default set: the cross-session and messaging tools (`SendMessage`, `ListAgents`, `PushNotification`), triggers and scheduling (`RemoteTrigger`, `CronCreate`, `CronDelete`, `CronList`, `ScheduleWakeup`), remote and sync tools (`DesignSync`, `Workflow`, `ReportFindings`), web access (`WebFetch`, `WebSearch`), agent spawning and background work (`Task`, `TaskStop`, `Monitor`), worktrees and plan mode (`EnterWorktree`, `ExitWorktree`, `EnterPlanMode`, `ExitPlanMode`), and the rest (`AskUserQuestion`, `NotebookEdit`, `Skill`, `ToolSearch`). `--disallowedTools` wasn't tested in the spike, so it's a second layer, and S1 checks it.
   167	     - **The adapter checks every `init`** (Claude re-sends it on every turn): `init.tools` must be a subset of the allowlist. Otherwise the start fails (first `init`) or the session is stopped (a later one), and the agent goes to Needs you. `init` arrives only after the first user line, about 40 ms after it in the spike and before the model's first reply. On a failed check the stop is **fast**, not the graceful stop sequence: the adapter at once sends an in-band `interrupt` and answers every `can_use_tool` from then on with a deny, and the `Session` returns `Abort`, so the pump runs the **fast stop** (no checkpoint turn, no wait on stdin; see "Processes and safety"). S1 confirms the order of `init` and the first reply. So a Claude release that adds a tool, or ignores a flag, never gets a tool call allowed with it.
   168	     - **Remote control stays off** (rev 3.4): Claude's `initialize` reports `remote_control_available: true` in every run. The adapter never sends a request that turns remote control on, and the start fails if the session reports remote control as active. S0 finds the setting or environment variable that turns it off, and the office sets it.
   169	     - A `can_use_tool` for a disallowed tool is always denied. One for a tool the adapter doesn't know is escalation `unknown` (decision 7).
   170	     - **Web access is off by default.** A later per-agent policy may enable `WebFetch` and `WebSearch` with a domain allowlist; that's not in phase 1.
   171	     - Bash's own background mode (`run_in_background`) is turned off with an office-set switch, `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1`, which S1 verifies (see "S0 checks and fallbacks").
   172	     - Codex and Antigravity get the same rule where they have such tools: S0 lists each runtime's built-in tools (Codex's web search, say), and the adapter pins its allowlist the runtime's way. Fallback: a runtime whose risky built-in tools can't be turned off isn't office-run.
   173	   - **Auth stays in each runtime's own store.** The office never puts API keys in an agent's environment. API-key support, when it's added, goes through each runtime's own credential mechanism.
   174	7. **Approvals go to the person, never silently lost.** In headless mode all three runtimes deny or soft-deny actions that need approval. The adapters bridge approval requests into the office:
   175	   - Claude: `--permission-prompt-tool stdio` and `can_use_tool` control requests. The flag is required: without it no request arrives, and the action is denied.
   176	   - Codex: `item/*/requestApproval`.
   177	   - Antigravity: ACP `session/request_permission`.
   178	
   179	   The office answers from the agent's **permission policy** (what's allowed without asking), and asks the owner in **Needs you** for anything else. Each runtime's own allow rules and sandbox are set from the same policy as a first line of defence, except allow rules for file-writing tools, which the office applies itself so that every write reaches its check (rev 3.3, below).
   180	   - **Escalating approvals (contract review of `org-runtime`, 2026-11-08):** every approval request carries a required `escalation`: `none`, `sandbox_bypass` (e.g. a Codex command asking to run unsandboxed), `permission_change` (Claude `ExitPlanMode`, an ACP mode switch) or `unknown`. The office ALWAYS DENIES `sandbox_bypass`: the fixed denies win, with no policy or owner override in phase 1. It NEVER answers `permission_change` or `unknown` from policy: they always go to the owner in Needs you with a clear warning (a request for a disallowed tool is denied at once instead; see Claude's mapping below). Adapters must set the field; an unrecognised approval kind is `unknown`.
   181	     - **It's carried end to end** (rev 3.3): the Approval record and `approval.requested` carry `escalation`, so the app can show the warning.
   182	     - **No standing rule for an escalated approval.** `approval.answer` refuses `allow_always` and `scope` on an approval whose escalation isn't `none` (`invalid_request`, reason `escalated`): the owner can only allow it once or deny it. `permission_policy.set` refuses an allow rule for a tool that always escalates (`ExitPlanMode`, `EnterPlanMode`, a mode switch; reason `escalating_tool`). And the office never writes such a tool into a runtime's own allow rules, so a runtime can't allow it by itself, without a request.
   183	     - **Claude's mapping** (every Claude request is a `can_use_tool`, so it's by tool name and input): `Bash` with `input.dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true` is `sandbox_bypass` (`allowUnsandboxedCommands: false` already refuses it; this is the second line); `ExitPlanMode` and `EnterPlanMode` are `permission_change`; a tool on the disallowed list is denied at once, and **that beats the mapping**: the plan-mode tools are disallowed, so a request for one is denied at once and recorded with escalation `permission_change`, never sent to Needs you; any other tool name outside the adapter's known list is `unknown`; the allowlisted tools are `none`.

Fallback: if they load, it's a documented limit like `~/.gemini`, and the owner is told when they enable that runtime. 834 - **`gh` with the session's own `GH_CONFIG_DIR`** (rev 3.3: an empty folder in the session's `TMPDIR`, removed when the session ends, since tools can't read the runtime dir): `gh` works through `agent-os gh-token`. It holds no login of the user's, and no other employee's session sees it, so no fallback is needed for safety. 835 - **Claude's sandbox deny lists accept wildcards** (rev 3.4): the `*` and `**` patterns this design writes (`offices/*/office.lock`, `offices//**` and the like) are honored by the sandbox for reads and writes, from Bash. The spike used only literal paths. Fallback: the office expands every pattern into literal paths at start (it knows every office and file), and the start fails if it can't. 836 - **Remote control off:** the setting or environment variable that keeps Claude's remote control off in an office-run session, and that `initialize` then shows it off. Fallback: Claude isn't office-run until it's found. 837 838 Tests at every step use a **fake runtime** (a test binary that speaks each recorded protocol), so CI never calls a model. The one smoke test per runtime is **opt-in**: it needs a secret and is off by default. 839

CREATE TABLE provider_connections (
organization_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(id),
  id TEXT NOT NULL,
  schema_version INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (schema_version = 1),
  revision INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (revision >= 1),
key TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(key)>0),
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  provider_type TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(provider_type)>0),
  auth_mode TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (auth_mode IN ('subscription_cli','api_key','cloud_iam')),
  subscription_identity TEXT CHECK (subscription_identity IS NULL OR length(trim(subscription_identity))>0),
  runtime_driver TEXT NOT NULL,
  endpoint_url TEXT,
  enabled INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK (enabled IN (0,1)),
  archived INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (archived IN (0,1)),
  max_concurrent_turns INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK (max_concurrent_turns>=1),
  created_at TEXT,
  created_by_kind TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'unknown' CHECK (created_by_kind IN ('employee','owner','system','unknown')),
  created_by_id TEXT,
  updated_at TEXT,
  updated_by_kind TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'unknown' CHECK (updated_by_kind IN ('employee','owner','system','unknown')),
  updated_by_id TEXT,
  PRIMARY KEY (organization_id,id),
UNIQUE (organization_id,key),
  UNIQUE (organization_id,provider_type,subscription_identity),
  CHECK (auth_mode<>'subscription_cli' OR subscription_identity IS NOT NULL),
  CHECK ((created_by_kind = 'employee' AND created_by_id IS NOT NULL) OR (created_by_kind <> 'employee' AND created_by_id IS NULL)),
  CHECK ((updated_by_kind = 'employee' AND updated_by_id IS NOT NULL) OR (updated_by_kind <> 'employee' AND updated_by_id IS NULL)),
  FOREIGN KEY (organization_id,created_by_id) REFERENCES employees(organization_id,id) DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED,
  FOREIGN KEY (organization_id,updated_by_id) REFERENCES employees(organization_id,id) DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED
) STRICT;

CREATE TRIGGER registered_subscription_cannot_be_replaced
BEFORE INSERT ON provider_connections
WHEN EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM provider_connections p
  WHERE p.organization_id=NEW.organization_id AND p.subscription_identity IS NOT NULL
    AND (p.id=NEW.id OR p.key=NEW.key OR
      (p.provider_type=NEW.provider_type AND p.subscription_identity=NEW.subscription_identity)))
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT,'registered subscription cannot be replaced; resolve existing connection'); END;

CREATE TRIGGER registered_subscription_cannot_be_displaced
BEFORE UPDATE ON provider_connections
WHEN EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM provider_connections p
  WHERE p.organization_id=NEW.organization_id AND p.subscription_identity IS NOT NULL
    AND NOT (p.organization_id=OLD.organization_id AND p.id=OLD.id)
    AND (p.id=NEW.id OR p.key=NEW.key OR
      (p.provider_type=NEW.provider_type AND p.subscription_identity=NEW.subscription_identity)))
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT,'registered subscription cannot be displaced by another connection'); END;

CREATE TRIGGER registered_subscription_identity_is_immutable
BEFORE UPDATE OF provider_type,subscription_identity ON provider_connections
WHEN OLD.subscription_identity IS NOT NULL AND
  (NEW.provider_type IS NOT OLD.provider_type OR NEW.subscription_identity IS NOT OLD.subscription_identity)
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT,'registered subscription identity is immutable'); END;

CREATE TABLE model_profiles (
organization_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(id),
  id TEXT NOT NULL,
  schema_version INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (schema_version = 1),
  revision INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (revision >= 1),
key TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(key)>0),
  name TEXT NOT NULL,

description TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  is_auto_generated INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (is_auto_generated IN (0,1)),
  generated_for_connection_id TEXT,
  archived INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (archived IN (0,1)),
  created_at TEXT,
  created_by_kind TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'unknown' CHECK (created_by_kind IN ('employee','owner','system','unknown')),
  created_by_id TEXT,
  updated_at TEXT,
  updated_by_kind TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'unknown' CHECK (updated_by_kind IN ('employee','owner','system','unknown')),
  updated_by_id TEXT,
  PRIMARY KEY (organization_id,id),
UNIQUE (organization_id,key),
  UNIQUE (organization_id,generated_for_connection_id),
  CHECK ((is_auto_generated=1 AND generated_for_connection_id IS NOT NULL) OR (is_auto_generated=0 AND generated_for_connection_id IS NULL)),
  FOREIGN KEY (organization_id,generated_for_connection_id) REFERENCES provider_connections(organization_id,id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  CHECK ((created_by_kind = 'employee' AND created_by_id IS NOT NULL) OR (created_by_kind <> 'employee' AND created_by_id IS NULL)),
  CHECK ((updated_by_kind = 'employee' AND updated_by_id IS NOT NULL) OR (updated_by_kind <> 'employee' AND updated_by_id IS NULL)),
  FOREIGN KEY (organization_id,created_by_id) REFERENCES employees(organization_id,id) DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED,
  FOREIGN KEY (organization_id,updated_by_id) REFERENCES employees(organization_id,id) DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED
) STRICT;

CREATE TABLE model_profile_connections (
organization_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  model_profile_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  connection_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  priority INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (priority BETWEEN 1 AND 64),
  PRIMARY KEY (organization_id,model_profile_id,connection_id),
  UNIQUE (organization_id,model_profile_id,priority),
  FOREIGN KEY (organization_id,model_profile_id) REFERENCES model_profiles(organization_id,id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  FOREIGN KEY (organization_id,connection_id) REFERENCES provider_connections(organization_id,id) ON DELETE RESTRICT
) STRICT;

CREATE TABLE agent_execution_configs (
organization_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(id),
  employee_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  schema_version INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (schema_version = 1),
  revision INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (revision >= 1),
model_profile_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  model_id TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(model_id)>0),
  system_prompt_markdown TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(system_prompt_markdown)>0),
  tools_config_json TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]' CHECK (json_valid(tools_config_json) AND json_type(tools_config_json)='array'),
  enabled INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK (enabled IN (0,1)),
  created_at TEXT,
  created_by_kind TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'unknown' CHECK (created_by_kind IN ('employee','owner','system','unknown')),
  created_by_id TEXT,
  updated_at TEXT,
  updated_by_kind TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'unknown' CHECK (updated_by_kind IN ('employee','owner','system','unknown')),
  updated_by_id TEXT,
  PRIMARY KEY (organization_id,employee_id),
FOREIGN KEY (organization_id,employee_id) REFERENCES employees(organization_id,id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  FOREIGN KEY (organization_id,model_profile_id) REFERENCES model_profiles(organization_id,id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  CHECK ((created_by_kind = 'employee' AND created_by_id IS NOT NULL) OR (created_by_kind <> 'employee' AND created_by_id IS NULL)),
  CHECK ((updated_by_kind = 'employee' AND updated_by_id IS NOT NULL) OR (updated_by_kind <> 'employee' AND updated_by_id IS NULL)),
  FOREIGN KEY (organization_id,created_by_id) REFERENCES employees(organization_id,id) DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED,
  FOREIGN KEY (organization_id,updated_by_id) REFERENCES employees(organization_id,id) DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED
) STRICT;

CREATE TABLE office_connection_bindings (
organization_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  office_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  connection_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  revision INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (revision>=1),
  auth_context_ref TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(auth_context_ref)>0),
  runtime_binary_path TEXT,
  account_identity_ref TEXT,
  updated_at TEXT NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (organization_id,office_id,connection_id),
  FOREIGN KEY (organization_id,office_id) REFERENCES offices(organization_id,id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  FOREIGN KEY (organization_id,connection_id) REFERENCES provider_connections(organization_id,id) ON DELETE RESTRICT
) STRICT;

CREATE TABLE office_connection_state (
organization_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  office_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  connection_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('unknown','ready','auth_expired','unavailable')),
  binding_revision INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (binding_revision>=1),
  driver_version TEXT,
  observed_at TEXT,
  valid_until TEXT,
  issue_code TEXT,
  PRIMARY KEY (organization_id,office_id,connection_id),
  CHECK (status<>'ready' OR (driver_version IS NOT NULL AND observed_at IS NOT NULL AND valid_until IS NOT NULL)),
  FOREIGN KEY (organization_id,office_id,connection_id) REFERENCES office_connection_bindings(organization_id,office_id,connection_id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

CREATE TABLE office_connection_models (
organization_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  office_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  connection_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  model_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  driver_model_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  entitlement TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (entitlement IN ('confirmed','denied','unknown')),
  capabilities_json TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}' CHECK (json_valid(capabilities_json) AND json_type(capabilities_json)='object'),
  observed_at TEXT NOT NULL,
  valid_until TEXT NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (organization_id,office_id,connection_id,model_id),
  FOREIGN KEY (organization_id,office_id,connection_id) REFERENCES office_connection_bindings(organization_id,office_id,connection_id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

CREATE TABLE connection_quota_state (
organization_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  connection_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  scope_key TEXT NOT NULL,
  model_id TEXT,
  status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('unknown','open','cooldown')),

  observed_by_office_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  coordinator_generation INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (coordinator_generation>=1),
  PRIMARY KEY (organization_id,connection_id,scope_key),
  CHECK ((model_id IS NULL AND scope_key='connection') OR (model_id IS NOT NULL AND scope_key='model:'||model_id)),
  CHECK (status<>'cooldown' OR cooldown_until IS NOT NULL),
  FOREIGN KEY (organization_id,connection_id) REFERENCES provider_connections(organization_id,id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  FOREIGN KEY (organization_id,observed_by_office_id) REFERENCES offices(organization_id,id) ON DELETE RESTRICT
) STRICT;

CREATE TABLE connection_turn_permits (

  UNIQUE (organization_id,id,connection_id,employee_id,office_id,placement_generation,model_id),
  FOREIGN KEY (organization_id,connection_id) REFERENCES provider_connections(organization_id,id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  FOREIGN KEY (organization_id,office_id) REFERENCES offices(organization_id,id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  FOREIGN KEY (organization_id,employee_id) REFERENCES employees(organization_id,id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

  outcome TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (outcome IN ('accepted','rejected')),

  recorded_at TEXT NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (organization_id,office_id,operation_id),
  FOREIGN KEY (organization_id,office_id) REFERENCES offices(organization_id,id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  FOREIGN KEY (organization_id,employee_id) REFERENCES employees(organization_id,id) ON DELETE RESTRICT
) STRICT;

CREATE TRIGGER placement_generation_must_advance BEFORE UPDATE ON agent_placements
WHEN NEW.placement_generation<OLD.placement_generation OR (NEW.office_id<>OLD.office_id AND NEW.placement_generation<=OLD.placement_generation)
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT,'office changes require a newer placement generation'); END;
CREATE INDEX agent_configs_by_profile ON agent_execution_configs(organization_id,model_profile_id);
CREATE INDEX profiles_by_connection ON model_profile_connections(organization_id,connection_id);
CREATE INDEX attempts_by_turn ON agent_execution_attempts(organization_id,turn_id,state);
CREATE INDEX permits_by_connection ON connection_turn_permits(organization_id,connection_id,state);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX one_open_turn_per_agent ON agent_execution_turns(organization_id,employee_id)
WHERE status IN ('accepted','running','switching','blocked','recovery_required');
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX one_owned_main_process ON agent_process_instances(organization_id,employee_id)
WHERE state<>'gone';
CREATE TRIGGER agent_config_requires_agent BEFORE INSERT ON agent_execution_configs
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT,'execution config requires an agent employee') WHERE EXISTS (
 SELECT 1 FROM employees e WHERE e.organization_id=NEW.organization_id AND e.id=NEW.employee_id AND e.kind<>'agent'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER agent_config_update_requires_agent BEFORE UPDATE OF employee_id,organization_id ON agent_execution_configs
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT,'execution config requires an agent employee') WHERE EXISTS (
 SELECT 1 FROM employees e WHERE e.organization_id=NEW.organization_id AND e.id=NEW.employee_id AND e.kind<>'agent'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER configured_employee_stays_agent BEFORE UPDATE OF kind ON employees
WHEN NEW.kind<>'agent' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM agent_execution_configs c WHERE c.organization_id=OLD.organization_id AND c.employee_id=OLD.id)
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT,'configured employee must remain an agent'); END;

CREATE VIEW model_profile_model_union AS
SELECT m.organization_id,m.office_id,p.model_profile_id,m.model_id,
 COUNT(*) AS supporting_connections,MIN(p.priority) AS first_priority
FROM model_profile_connections p JOIN office_connection_models m
 ON m.organization_id=p.organization_id AND m.connection_id=p.connection_id
WHERE m.entitlement='confirmed'
GROUP BY m.organization_id,m.office_id,p.model_profile_id,m.model_id;

The sketch distinguishes present libraries from proposed packages. Present code
and its tests describe the implemented contract, not completion of the selected
organization-data schema, runtime routing or replication-source migration. Reassess
physical extraction during implementation rather than creating empty packages.
The agentic-org application composes org-host. Its setup command and serve process share library behavior; there is no additional host/updater daemon.

`org-office` currently deliberately combines domain behavior and storage. Keep its
private store and single-writer invariant. Logical domain ownership does not require
separate databases, writers, or public SQL repositories. Its store adapters implement
consumer-owned contracts such as the work and messaging ports. Keep transactions,
deduplication, outbox writes, and sequence allocation atomic as their designs require.

Source dependencies point from adapters/composition toward policies and contracts:

```text
instance gateway -> typed authorized host/office client operations
per-office server -> public use-case APIs / selected runtime and sync adapters
office storage implementations -> work and messaging ports
work and messaging -> their required protocol vocabulary
session coordinator -> employee policy + runtime contracts
harness adapters -> runtime contracts
```

The standalone design chooses one `agentic-org-web` process per instance for browser
HTTP/TLS, routing all authorized HQ organizations on the same listener. The host
keeps office keys/catalog provisioning; each `agentic-org-office` remains one office worker.
Create organization requires instance-admin authority, not just organization
ownership. Keep gateway endpoint code focused on principal authorization, decoding,
typed public operations and result mapping; never return an office key to it. A small HTTP adapter crate remains an option
when its dependency boundary or actual callers justify extraction. Do not depend on
one runnable application's library from another to assemble the service.

## 5. Shared functionality: upload, validation, and hashes

Use the narrowest meaningful owner. Feature-specific avatar validation belongs to
the avatar feature; rules shared by one domain belong to its internal policy module.
A genuinely reusable upload capability can have a `files` owner with a public API.
The following is an **illustrative future example**, not an added v1 upload requirement:

```text
office implementation/
  files/
    mod.rs                           # Public file operations
    features/upload.rs
    policy.rs                        # Common file constraints
    content_digest.rs                # File identity semantics, if required
    ports.rs                         # Storage capability contract
    adapters/local_storage.rs
  employees/features/upload_avatar.rs
  projects/features/attach_document.rs

apps/agentic-org-ui/src/lib/
  components/ui/FilePicker.svelte
  components/ui/UploadProgress.svelte
  modules/files/upload/UploadPanel.svelte
  modules/files/api.ts
  modules/employees/features/upload-avatar/AvatarEditor.svelte
```

Employee/project operations own their business permissions and restrictions; file
operations enforce their common invariants and own storage integration. Consumers
call public operations rather than reconstructing a sequence of internal helpers.
Client checks provide feedback; Rust enforces policy on received content. Share
policy metadata, contracts, and test vectors across runtimes where useful.

Use an established hashing library, such as the workspace's `sha2`, for the basic
algorithm. File fingerprints, retry-deduplication hashes, and message-content hashes
have different canonicalization and compatibility contracts. Keep those semantics
with their owners. Existing `org-work::params_hash` and `org-mailbox::content_hash`
must not be merged merely because both use hashing. Extract a shared digest type or
module only for deliberately identical semantics; a separate crate needs a real
package-level purpose. Avoid a generic shared/Common/Utils dumping ground.

## 6. End-to-end slice example: set employee goal

1. The Svelte feature captures the goal and displays submission/outcome state.
2. HQ authenticates the human, authorizes the employee scope, and validates the
   operation ID and expected version through a typed HTTP operation.
3. The command reaches the owning office through an explicit, authorized contract.
4. The employee module validates and persists the update through office-owned storage.
5. Local session coordination delivers the current goal at a safe boundary under
   the single-main-session, takeover, and bounded reminder rules.
6. The browser observes the command outcome and runtime delivery/freshness separately.

A new goal change to an office known to be offline is rejected before admission,
with no goal write or queued update; keep the unsaved draft. A forwarded request
with unknown outcome uses Pending confirmation and the same operation ID for lookup/
retry, as [employee-supervision.md](employee-supervision.md#goal-command-admission-and-offline-behavior)
specifies. Acceptance does not prove completion or that a model read the goal. Browser disconnection does
not end durable work. Pause is a durable HQ status command even for an offline office, with runtime
stop pending until acknowledged, as the employee and session designs require; renaming/moving code does not transfer that authority.

| Step | Source-to-target work | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Contract/owner inventory | Map every moved public API, test fixture, transport caller, and baseline-only path; coordinate under AGENTS.md | Preserve documented behavior and acceptance IDs; identify unimplemented surfaces |

| 3. Domain organization | Move organization/employee/process behavior into cohesive modules; group work and messaging use cases in their existing crates | Preserve public compatibility where retained, visibility, transactions, invariants, and acyclic source direction |
| 4. Real feature integration | Implement each retained use case through its canonical Rust behavior, typed HTTP operation, Svelte feature, and meaningful tests | Replace production mock selection and Tauri callers in the same supported feature change; show explicit unavailable state for missing operations |
| 5. Desktop deletion and packaging | Apply the removal inventory; delete Tauri-only sources/dependencies and regenerate lockfiles | Preserve host key custody, private worker launch, local agent IPC, licensed UI location, bounded resources, and complete release payloads |
| 6. Runtime/federation acceptance | Implement the planned session/harness/sync capabilities according to their designs | Run platform, isolation, reconnect, durability, and cleanup evidence required by PR #5 |

Keep implementation commits buildable. Naming, domain extraction, HTTP integration,
and deletion may be grouped where callers require an atomic change. No old desktop
data migration or Tauri compatibility adapter is required. New standalone upgrades
still require their own schema/version compatibility handling.

Evaluate coupling at both workspace-package and logical-domain levels. For example,
the inspected normal internal package dependencies give `org-work` Ce=1,
`org-mailbox` Ce=1, and `org-office` Ce=2, excluding external/dev dependencies.

boundaries are correct. Reassess when wiring new ports and cross-domain workflows.

Completion requires consistent target names, intentional public APIs, no new source
cycles, authoritative server rules, licensed UI containment, no production mock
fallback, and preserved office/process/storage semantics. Run repository formatting,
Clippy, Rust tests, frontend checks/tests/build, and relevant browser tests for the
actual implementation. Validate docs/links and preserved acceptance IDs for this
documentation proposal; do not claim source moves or runtime checks here.
